learningObjectives: Structure an end-to-end scenario using the Precondition / Process / Post condition pattern.
Extract shared steps into a TestStepLibrary as a reusable TestStep block.
Buffer a value produced at runtime and consume it in a later TestStep.
Combine web automation with the PDF Engine in a single business flow.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What the Grand Scenario is for

elements.term: From isolated lessons to one business process
elements.description: This local worked scenario combines login, book ordering, invoice download and logout to illustrate cross-technology test design. The original Academy base subset and exact exercise sequence have not been inspected, so the labels and steps below are an independent teaching example, not a certified reproduction.

elements.text: Use available scanned Modules or scan the application yourself. The claimed original Grand Scenario subset folders and supplied Module inventory have not been verified; compare your workspace with the official exercise before following its exact instructions.

bulletPoints: The capstone: one business flow, several engines, structured properly.

elements.term: Why the scenario is split into three
elements.description: In this local example, Precondition establishes the starting session, Process exercises ordering and Post condition verifies logout and closes the browser. These names are a design choice, not a Tosca-required folder structure. Session cleanup does not delete orders or restore all business data.

elements.title: The three TestCases
items: Precondition — 'Login to web shop': gets a logged-in session, then verifies the login succeeded.
Process — 'Order fiction book and pay on delivery': the business flow being tested.
Post condition — 'Logout from the web shop': logs out, verifies the logout, and closes the browser instance.

elements.text: Arrange cleanup to run on relevant failure paths as well as success. Three sequential TestCases do not themselves guarantee that logout or close executes after an earlier failure. Closing a browser releases the session; it does not undo the order.

bulletPoints: Precondition = get to the starting state. Process = what is under test. Post condition = clean up and verify the cleanup.

elements.term: The 'Login to web shop' reusable block
elements.description: Logging in is needed by the Precondition and would be needed by any other scenario against the same shop. Rather than duplicating those steps, the scenario keeps a TestStepLibrary containing a reusable TestStep block named 'Login to web shop', made up of three steps: Open demo web shop, Click on log in link, and Provide log in details.

References to a Reusable TestStepBlock share centrally maintained steps; changes affect all linked references. A resolved reference becomes an independent copy, so it no longer receives those changes. Updating shared steps still requires validating callers and their assertions.

elements.text: This example keeps successful-login verification with the caller. That is a design choice: reusable blocks may also contain verification TestSteps when those assertions are genuinely shared.

bulletPoints: TestStepLibrary → reusable TestStep block 'Login to web shop' (open · click log in · provide details).
Caller-specific verification can remain outside the block; shared assertions can also be reused.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Process TestCase, step by step

elements.description: This independent flow groups ordering into three folders for readability. A folder label helps locate a phase but does not prove the root cause of a failure or verify the original Academy sequence.

elements.title: Navigation to product
items: Click on show details for fiction

elements.title: Check out process
items: Accept terms of service and proceed to checkout

elements.title: Verification of order creation
items: Verify order and buffer order no

bulletPoints: Grouping TestSteps into folders turns a 14-step flow into three readable phases.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The two techniques that make it work

elements.description: Capture the current order identifier with ActionMode Buffer, or use XBuffer within a verified message to extract its dynamic part. Later steps read {B[OrderID]}. Do not assume the identifier differs on every run; use the value actually produced by the application.

Downloading the invoice is a browser/file operation, not automatic PDF verification. Verify the file is available, then use PDF Modules for the chosen checks. Content extraction and reference comparison are distinct operations. Configure explicit page/area exclusions only for allowed differences; verify the captured order identifier separately rather than hiding an important mismatch.

elements.text: Tosca supports appropriate engine Modules within a business flow, subject to their prerequisites and compatibility. Reuse and buffering do not guarantee that every engine combination or document check works without configuration.
Complete the official Academy capstone using its supplied materials. This local example does not verify the original subset, figures, exact checkout order or PDF assertions.

bulletPoints: Capture and consume the actual runtime identifier; do not rely on a previous run’s value.
Downloading a PDF does not verify it; add explicit document assertions and justified comparison exclusions.

examPitfalls.title: Putting login steps inside the Process TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Building one long TestCase that logs in, orders, and logs out, because it mirrors what a user does.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate setup, the business behavior and cleanup when that improves clarity. A single TestCase can also be valid; shared steps can be extracted without mandating three TestCases. Ensure the execution strategy handles failure cleanup.

examPitfalls.title: Hard-coding the order number
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reading an order number from a manual run and typing it into the 'navigate to order details' step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Capture the current generated identifier and reference that value later. Buffering avoids assuming a known prior identifier; it does not establish that IDs differ on every execution.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting to close the browser instance in the Post condition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Logging out and considering the cleanup complete.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: This example logs out, verifies logout and closes the browser. Ensure cleanup also runs on relevant failures; browser cleanup does not delete orders or restore business data.

examPitfalls.title: Duplicating the login steps instead of reusing the library block
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Copying the three login TestSteps into each TestCase that needs a logged-in session.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: References to a Reusable TestStepBlock share centrally maintained steps; changes affect all linked references. A resolved reference becomes an independent copy, so it no longer receives those changes. Updating shared steps still requires validating callers and their assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Treating the PDF invoice as out of scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ending the verification at the order confirmation page because the invoice is 'just a document'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Downloading the invoice is a browser/file operation, not automatic PDF verification. Verify the file is available, then use PDF Modules for the chosen checks. Content extraction and reference comparison are distinct operations. Configure explicit page/area exclusions only for allowed differences; verify the captured order identifier separately rather than hiding an important mismatch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does this local worked example separate setup, ordering and cleanup?

options.text: As a single TestCase covering the whole flow.
Into Precondition, Process, and Post condition.
By engine — one TestCase per technology.
Into Smoke, Regression, and One-time tests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Setup, the thing under test, and cleanup.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario separates Precondition (log in), Process (order the book and pay on delivery), and Post condition (log out, verify, close the browser). This keeps setup and cleanup distinct from the behaviour actually being tested.

optionExplanations.A: A single TestCase can be valid, but this example chooses separate setup, ordering and cleanup.
optionExplanations.B: These three phases describe the local worked example, not a mandatory Tosca or verified Academy structure.
optionExplanations.C: The example groups business phases rather than splitting solely by engine.
optionExplanations.D: These are test-suite categories, not the example’s setup/process/cleanup phases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The step 'Verify order and buffer order no' captures the order number into a buffer. Why is this necessary?

options.text: To make the TestCase run faster.
Because later steps need the actual runtime identifier, rather than a value copied from a prior run.
Because buffers are required in every Tosca TestCase.
To satisfy the PDF Engine's anchor requirements.

practiceQuiz.hint: The value does not exist until the application creates it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Buffering captures the current order identifier for later use. The application decides its allocation behavior; the test should not assume every execution produces a different identifier.

optionExplanations.A: Buffering supplies the actual runtime value; it does not inherently promise faster execution.
optionExplanations.B: Capture the current identifier and consume it later rather than using a value from a previous run.
optionExplanations.C: Buffers are useful when a later step needs captured values, not mandatory in every TestCase.
optionExplanations.D: Capturing an order identifier is distinct from configuring PDF anchor identification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In this local example, where are the shared login actions placed for central maintenance?

options.text: Duplicated in each TestCase that needs them, for independence.
In a TestStepLibrary as a reusable TestStep block named 'Login to web shop', so there is a single point of maintenance.
In the Post condition, so they run last.
In a Module, since Modules are the reuse mechanism for TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.hint: The same centralised-maintenance argument behind Classes and Libraries.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The example uses a Reusable TestStepBlock in a TestStepLibrary. Changes affect linked references; resolved copies are independent and require their own updates.

optionExplanations.A: Independent copies require separate maintenance and do not provide linked reuse.
optionExplanations.B: A TestStepLibrary’s Reusable TestStepBlock centrally maintains linked references. Resolved copies are no longer linked.
optionExplanations.C: Login establishes the starting session in this example; it is not the logout cleanup action.
optionExplanations.D: Modules describe automation interfaces; the TestStepLibrary reuses sequences of TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After downloading a PDF invoice in this worked example, which approach verifies the document instead of merely proving a download?

options.text: The Excel Engine, using TBox Excel 1:1 File Compare.
Use PDF Modules for explicit content or comparison checks, configure only justified exclusions, and verify the runtime order identifier separately.
The Mail Engine, since invoices are emailed.
No engine change is needed; XBrowser handles the PDF.

practiceQuiz.hint: Download completion and invoice correctness are different assertions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Downloading the invoice is a browser/file operation, not automatic PDF verification. Verify the file is available, then use PDF Modules for the chosen checks. Content extraction and reference comparison are distinct operations. Configure explicit page/area exclusions only for allowed differences; verify the captured order identifier separately rather than hiding an important mismatch.

optionExplanations.A: Excel file comparison is not PDF invoice verification.
optionExplanations.B: Add explicit PDF assertions after the download. Allowed exclusions must not hide the dynamic identifier check.
optionExplanations.C: A downloaded PDF need not arrive through email; Mail Modules are not a PDF-content verifier.
optionExplanations.D: A browser download alone does not establish document content correctness.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which three session-cleanup actions are chosen in this local worked example?

options.text: Log out from web shop, verify successful logout, close the demo web shop browser instance.
Log out and nothing further — the browser closes automatically.
Delete the order, log out, clear the cart.
Verify the invoice, log out, archive the PDF.

practiceQuiz.hint: Cleanup includes verifying that the cleanup itself worked.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The example chooses logout, logout verification and browser closure. This is not complete business-data rollback or a guarantee that cleanup executes after failures.

optionExplanations.A: These are the session-cleanup actions selected by the local example. They do not restore all business data.
optionExplanations.B: This example explicitly closes the browser; logout does not guarantee automatic browser closure.
optionExplanations.C: Order deletion/cart cleanup are different business-data operations not chosen here.
optionExplanations.D: Invoice checks and archiving are not the example’s logout/close sequence.

quickRecap.value: Independent local purchase-flow example; original Academy subset/sequence unverified.
Precondition (login) → Process (order fiction book, pay on delivery) → Post condition (logout).
Linked Reusable TestStepBlock references share updates; resolved copies do not. Caller/shared assertions are design choices.
Navigation to product → Check out process → Verification of order creation.
'Verify order and buffer order no' captures the runtime order number for the later navigation step.
Download is not PDF verification; add content/comparison assertions and validate the dynamic order identifier.
Logout · verify logout · close browser; ensure failure-path cleanup and separate business-data rollback as needed.
Original supplied Module inventory not inspected; compare your workspace with official Academy materials.
